instruction: Correct the chemical notation in the field note by lowering every numeral in each CO2 formula to subscript. Keep all wording unchanged.

states.value:
FIELD NOTE
CO2—Greenhouse Carbon
CARBON DIOXIDE MOVES CONTINUALLY BETWEEN THE AIR, PLANTS, WATER, AND SOIL. IN A GREENHOUSE, CO2 CAN SUPPORT PHOTOSYNTHESIS WHEN LIGHT, TEMPERATURE, AND MOISTURE ARE ALSO SUITABLE.
CO2 observations are most useful when they are read alongside airflow, light, temperature, and moisture conditions.
During daylight trials, technicians record CO2 near the plant canopy and again beside the ventilation outlet. Comparing these locations helps them recognize how airflow and plant activity influence the chamber.
A sudden rise in CO2 may reflect a dosing cycle, reduced ventilation, or a sensor that needs inspection. Staff confirm unusual readings against a second instrument before changing the greenhouse controls.
At the end of each shift, the team reviews the CO2 log alongside notes about light, temperature, irrigation, and fan operation. This context keeps a single measurement from being interpreted in isolation.
Before sharing the field note, check that every CO2 formula uses standard chemical notation. Consistent formatting makes CO2 references easier to scan in reports, handover notes, and training material.
Routine calibration notes record instrument status, weather conditions, door openings, and maintenance work. These details help later reviewers separate operational events from environmental changes.
